title: SSO proxy token synchronizer race causing missing journal entries / remediation plan
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: During a cross-region SSO proxy rollout two weeks ago we observed intermittent gaps in the audit journal where session grant/revoke events were not recorded for a subset of tokens. Root cause analysis identified a race between the token synchronizer worker and the journal writer under high burst scales: the synchronizer acked token propagation before journal persistence completed, leading to a window where downstream services treated tokens as valid while the canonical audit trail lacked entries. This ticket tracks the remediation tasks, design decisions, rollout plan, and verification steps.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Triage: Incident reported by SRE from alert 'audit-journal-missing-entries' during SSO rollout. Initial scope: ~0.2% token ops in eu-west-1 over a 3-hour window. Assigned to Ethan Li (security infra).

2025-02-15 - RCA sprint started. Reproduced race locally by ramping synchronizer concurrency + introducing artificial journal latency. Determined the synchronizer commit path signals success on write to remote cache before journal writer fsync completes.

2025-02-17 - Decision: implement two complementary mitigations: (A) change synchronizer to wait for journal ack (logical write-confirmation) for cross-region token operations; (B) decouple fast-path cache ack with a deferred 'visibility' flag on tokens to avoid adding latency to the happy path. Both chosen to reduce blast radius and maintain latency SLOs. Documented trade-offs in design doc link.
2025-02-20 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1852 implements ticket A (temporary strict ack). Marked as hotfix candidate. Added feature flag ssoproxy.strict_journal_ack.

2025-02-22 - Review feedback from Security (Priya Desai): request to add telemetry for write latencies and a histogram-based alert when journal latency > 200ms and outstanding unacked tokens > 100. Added to PR comments.

2025-02-24 - Parallel work: Implemented lightweight reconciliation sweep to backfill missing journal entries for the affected time window. Backfill script staged at tools/audit-backfill/runbook-ssoproxy-2025-02-24.sh. Backfill will run in dry-run mode first.

2025-02-25 - Canaries: Deployed hotfix (strict_journal_ack) behind FF to 10% of traffic in eu-west-1. Observed increase in median token issuance latency from 8ms to 14ms (within tolerated SLO). No additional missing journal alerts triggered in canary window. Monitoring dashboards updated.

2025-02-27 - Post-deploy verification: Dry-run backfill produced ~1.1k inferred events that were missing; manual sample validated against auth service logs. Decided to schedule full backfill during low-traffic maintenance window.

2025-03-01 - Security review: Completed threat analysis for the deferred visibility flag approach; concluded acceptable if combined with deterministic reconciliation and audit immutability guards. Action: follow-up ticket for deferred visibility design (ENG-90045).

2025-03-03 - Next steps: (1) Merge hotfix PR after one more security sign-off, (2) run full backfill during 2025-03-07 maintenance, (3) implement deferred visibility and telemetry, (4) update runbooks and SLOs. Assigned owners updated in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: No further missing-audit-entry alerts attributable to token synchronizer race across a 7-day observation window post-deploy.
Backfill completes successfully and all backfilled entries have corresponding validation hashes with auth logs for a 100-sample audit.
Telemetry added: histogram of journal write latency, gauge for outstanding unacked tokens, and alerting thresholds configured.
Runbook updated with steps to disable strict_journal_ack feature flag if regression observed and clear rollback plan.
